subject: Re: Request — ownership of third-party components & key access evidence
messages:
From: Jordan Price <security@galensec.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@medtech.io
Date: Sat, 1 Mar 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request — encryption key ownership + third-party inventory

Hi Karthik,

Galen is running a targeted SIG/CAIQ review with one of our joint customers (MedTech). They asked specifically for: 1) a current list of all subprocessors that may see unencrypted customer data in transit or at rest, 2) an architecture diagram showing where KMS/HSM keys are stored and who has admin access, and 3) sample audit logs showing key rotation / access events.

Can you provide a single package we can hand to their security team (CSV of subprocessors, short narrative about key ownership, and a diagram)? We prefer a secure link; if you have a DocuSign or signed attestation that would speed things up.

Target deadline: EOD Tue (3/4) if possible.

Thanks — we can loop in procurement if needed.

Jordan Price
Senior Security Analyst
Galen Security
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <security@galensec.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 1 Mar 2025 09:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request — encryption key ownership + third-party inventory

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the clear ask — we can assemble that package. Attaching a CSV export of our 3P inventory and a short manifest describing what each col means. High level notes below:

- Subprocessors: the CSV (redwood_thirdparty_inventory_2025-03.csv) includes all providers that process user data for inference, telemetry, logging, and customer-facing storage. Columns: name, function, region, data_access_type (e.g., encrypted-at-rest, has-kv-access), contract_start, soc2_attestation_link.
- Key ownership: Redwood by default uses customer-keyable KMS for dedicated/private installs; for hosted customers we manage envelope encryption keys in our KMS (AWS KMS in us-west-2) and maintain access via HSM-backed master keys. Customer-level data keys are rotated and wrapped with master keys. See attached diagram kms_keyflow_diagram.pdf.
- Audit sample: audit-log-sample-20250228.json shows a redacted example of key-rotate and admin-access entries.

We're including laura from Legal for attestation language and Soojin from Infra for the KMS/HSM details.

I'll upload the full package to a secure Drive link and share a DocuSign attestation we can sign if MedTech requires it. Expect the secure package by EOD Mon (3/3).

Regards,

Karthik Iyer
Director, Trust & Security
Redwood Inference
(karthik_iyer@redwood.com)

Attachments: redwood_thirdparty_inventory_2025-03.csv; kms_keyflow_diagram.pdf; audit-log-sample-20250228.json

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications from MedTech's security reviewer: 

1) For hosted customers, can you confirm whether long-term access to master keys is ever granted to a human operator outside of Redwood's HSM/KMS roles?
2) The CSV marks several analytics vendors as "has-kv-access" — can you confirm whether those vendors see any unencrypted PHI or whether data is pseudonymized before forwarding?

If you can reply with short one-line confirmations and indicate where in the diagram the key wrapping occurs, that will probably be sufficient. If you prefer, Soojin's note can be used for the technical statement.

Regards,
Jordan

Jordan,

Short answers inline below for MedTech's reviewer: 

1) Human access to master keys: No. Master keys are HSM-protected and access to them is controlled by a least-privilege KMS roles policy. We do not export raw master key material to humans or external vendors. Administrative operations (e.g., rotation) are performed via automated routines or gated workflows requiring multi-person approval; these actions produce audit events captured in KMS logs. (See kms_keyflow_diagram.pdf — master key box labeled "HSM (AWS KMS CMK)" and the note at step 4 about restricted admin API endpoints.)

2) Analytics vendors and PHI: Vendors marked as "has-kv-access" receive only tokenized/pseudonymized identifiers for analytics pipelines. We do not forward unencrypted PHI fields to analytics vendors for hosted customers. For Dedicated/Private deployments where customers bring their own keys, customers may configure different pipelines — those are called out in the CSV under "customer_managed_keys = true".

Additional evidence and next steps: 
- Shared secure bundle: https://drive.google.com/secure-share/1a2b3c-redwood-evidence (expires 7 days).
- DocuSign attestation template: DOCUSIGN:0x9f8e7d6c (if MedTech requires a signed statement we can route).
- If the reviewer wants a redacted KMS access audit for a custom time-window, we can provide it under NDA.

Laura — can you confirm whether the attestation language below is acceptable for Galen/MedTech?

---
Attestation: Redwood Inference maintains HSM-backed master keys for hosted customers and enforces role-based access controls for all key management operations. We do not permit human export of master key material and we rotate data-encryption keys on a 90-day schedule. Subprocessor access to customer data is governed by contractual clauses and technical controls limiting exposure to pseudonymized identifiers when applicable.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference

Soojin — any additional infra points to add?

Thanks,
Karthik
